steps: To determine the ancestral state of a trait, one must use an outgroup comparison.
An outgroup is a taxon that is closely related to the group under study but branched off earlier.
Comparing the trait in the study group to a more distantly related relative helps polarize the character state.
Option (B) describes the use of an outgroup to infer the ancestral condition.
Options (A), (C), and (D) do not provide a valid phylogenetic method for determining the ancestral state of the snake tongue.
